# Greenrock Innovations

> Climate technology company converting waste rock and weathered rock from Karnataka's quarrying sector into IS 383:2016 compliant manufactured sand and construction aggregates — approximately 70% lower carbon than primary-extraction equivalents. Operating under Karnataka's first Waste Rock Royalty Recycle Permit of its kind, from Gundlupet at the southern corridor of the Western Ghats.

Greenrock Innovations operates a network of automated, tech-enabled manufacturing facilities producing engineered sand and aggregates from reclaimed, weathered rock. The largest facility is Begur Sands Pvt. Ltd. in Gundlupet, Karnataka — the original engineering site where the closed-loop processing system was designed and validated. The model eliminates fresh extraction by processing waste material already generated by primary quarrying operations.

Every batch is independently tested at NABL-accredited laboratories. Process water is recirculated through a closed-loop hydrocyclone system (zero liquid discharge). Outputs are spec'd to IS 383:2016, IS 1542:1992, and MORTH references.

## Key facts

- Founded around the principle: discipline before scale. Original system engineered 2016–2024; commercial production scaled 2025.
- Carbon footprint per tonne of finished output: ~70% lower than conventional primary-extraction manufactured sand.
- Permits: Karnataka state Waste Rock Royalty Recycle Permit (first of its kind), Bureau Veritas certification, BIS-hallmarked output, Zero Liquid Discharge compliant.
- Process: super-primary jaw crushing → multi-deck vibrating screen segregation → vertical shaft impactor (VSI) shaping → closed-loop hydrocyclone classification + water reuse → PLC-governed auto-feeder & batch traceability → high-frequency dewatering screen.
- Output classes: M-Sand (IS 383 Zone II, structural concrete), P-Sand (IS 1542, plaster/finishing), Graded Aggregates (IS 383 coarse, 6/10/20 mm), Granite Fines (sub-grade, filler, asphalt).
- Location: Gundlupet, Chamarajanagar district, Karnataka, India — southern corridor of the Western Ghats.
- Corporate structure: Greenrock Innovations is the operating platform; Begur Sands Pvt. Ltd. is its largest facility and original engineering site.
- Domain: https://greenrockinnovations.earth — contact: hello@greenrockinnovations.earth

## Journal — Sustainable Construction Intelligence

- [The Hidden Cost of River Sand](https://greenrockinnovations.earth/journal/the-hidden-cost-of-river-sand) (Jan 2026): What India's construction boom is doing to its riverbeds — extraction scale, ecological cost, the manufactured-sand alternative.
- [M-Sand, P-Sand, G-Sand: Every Type of Manufactured Sand Explained](https://greenrockinnovations.earth/journal/manufactured-sand-types-complete-guide) (Apr 2026): IS 383:2016 gradation zones, applications, source rock effects, why specification matters.
- [Sand, Aggregates, Cement: What the Embodied Carbon Data Says](https://greenrockinnovations.earth/journal/embodied-carbon-construction-materials) (Apr 2026): Aggregate's missing place in carbon accounting; circular feedstock economics; EPD readiness.
- [Why Karnataka's Infrastructure Growth Cannot Afford to Ignore Its Biodiversity Footprint](https://greenrockinnovations.earth/journal/western-ghats-construction-biodiversity) (May 2026): Western Ghats hydrology, Gadgil/Kasturirangan frameworks, the waste-rock alternative.

## Topics this site authoritatively covers

- Manufactured sand (M-Sand) and IS 383:2016 specification
- Plastering sand (P-Sand) and IS 1542:1992
- Graded coarse aggregate, flakiness and elongation indices, crushing value
- Waste rock and weathered rock processing
- Closed-loop water recycling in mineral processing (Zero Liquid Discharge)
- Embodied carbon in construction aggregates and concrete
- River sand extraction impact on Indian river systems (Cauvery, Krishna, Godavari, Periyar)
- Western Ghats biodiversity and quarrying pressure (Gadgil report, Kasturirangan panel)
- Karnataka quarrying sector and Waste Rock Royalty Recycle Permits
- ESG-aligned construction supply chains and Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs)
- Vertical Shaft Impactor (VSI) technology and cubical particle shape engineering
- Hydrocyclone classification and fines recovery
